question: Gijón is a port in the TEN-T core network and its rail access must meet the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2024/1679 for freight by 2030: 740 m trains, P400 gauge, electrification at 25 kV and equipped with the European Rail Traffic Management System (ERTMS).

However, the Oviedo-Gijón renovation project put out to tender by Spain’s state-owned rail enterprise Adif, as part of the Plan de Cercanías (‘Local Transport Plan’), is limited to extending the gauge, and not including the 740 m, electrification or ERTMS, and its excludes the access branches to the quay (lines 150, 152 and 144), implemented by the port authority using the Iberian gauge.

In addition, the regulation set a deadline of 18 July 2026 for Member States to assess the core network lines eligible for migration to standard gauge (1 435 mm) or to justify their exclusion on the basis of a cost-benefit analysis. In view of the above: 1.

Has the Commission received the assessment submitted by Spain and does it include the Pola de Lena-Gijón axis? If not, does it have the cost-benefit analysis to justify not carrying out the migration?
Does the Commission believe that the Oviedo-Gijón project will meet the requirements of the core network by 2030?
What assurances does the Commission offer to ensure compliance and what consequences does it foresee if rail access to the port of Gijón does not meet these standards?
Supporter1
This question is supported by a Member other than the author: Borja Giménez Larraz (PPE).
